title: Simultaneous Survival-Difference Bands for a Small Target Trial with Locally Differing Sources
banked_reason: Below field floor: general review 6.7<7.4 and tier subfield. D0.5 math review FAIL; fold-balance, covariance, joint-process, and strict-gain findings remain unrepaired. Archive as an unverified draft; do not treat the headline as a sound theorem.
gap_reasons: The delivered package lacks the promised all-procedure minimax characterization or a replacement two-sided bracket, while the strict-gain result remains confined to a highly specialized construction; the general referee finds no bounded in-scope route to the field floor.

Under the allowed globally balanced but site-segregated two-fold map, the deterministic fallback gives θ_hat_ka=1 and eta_hat=0 rather than the asserted influence/KKT process; thus the stated uniform joint limit is false unless a per-stratum fold-balance (or randomized stratified-fold) assumption is added.

The claimed covariance representation is wrong: if E_0a,E_1a each have covariance 4S(s)S(t)R(s∧t), then (E_0a+E_1a)/2 has covariance 2S(s)S(t)R(s∧t), not that of 2S(t)B(R(t)); a domination argument could repair the conservative tail bound, but the displayed equality cannot.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed a corrected federated survival estimator and a specialized positive-radius strict-gain witness, but the all-procedure minimax characterization and two-sided transfer did not survive review. D0.5 judged the resulting package subfield rather than field and found counterexamples to the declared fold setup and a false covariance equality; the joint-process and strict-gain headlines remain unverified. This archive preserves the draft and review receipts for a possible repaired retry, not a sound theorem claim.
tldr: A small target trial region needs one simultaneous band for its identified treated-minus-control survival curve, while source regions may differ locally. The corrected same-curve estimator is computable from complete fold-resolved event-risk summaries and has a joint nonlinear Gaussian curve-and-weight limit. The proposed universal two-sided transfer is false on the fixed bounded tangent class: an exactly honest deterministic band can be strictly narrower than the invariant Gaussian lower benchmark, for every declared source-shift and target-mass radius satisfying the proved separation condition. Separately, the corrected estimator has a certified positive-radius, positive-penalty rectangle: its width is below 5.902, while every target-only band exceeds 5.94615.
gap: Published federated causal survival theory is pointwise at the aggregation step. Weak-alignment efficiency theory treats finite-dimensional misalignment, while published optimal-band results either use one source, restrict band shape, or optimize finite simulated paths; none supplies an exact local-law minimax value and two-sided all-action transfer for the complete right-censored multiplicative-intensity experiment with its censor and cell-law nuisance coordinates.
fill: The corrected estimator first gives a fold-indexed cellwise influence formula with an explicit target-anchor term, event-martingale term, risk and censor denominators, nuisance substitution, and total fallback. A Stieltjes reconstruction then maps the retained fold paths exactly to every empirical second moment in the direct quadratic and supplies the KKT limit used by the nonlinear process theorem. A reusable summary-action lemma proves losslessness for arbitrary randomized connected bands under the finite-cell multiplicative-intensity factorization. The central open task is the displayed two-sided transfer bound under \(\mathfrak S_j\) on the domain \(n\ge N_0\), including the explicit coverage and width debits \(E^c_{n,j}\) and \(E^w_{n,j}\). The rational witness \(\mathfrak W\) is supporting evidence; the all-procedure value, convergent certified bounds, feasible attainment, and open strict-gain region follow only after the transfer is established.
